caption: The image is a technical drawing of a chest of drawers rendered in black ink on a beige or off-white background. The drawing comprises three main views: a top-down rectangle showing the plan of the chest at the top left, a front elevation in the bottom left, and a side elevation to the right. The front elevation depicts four rows of drawers, each with geometric and ornamental designs including rectangular, triangular, and octagonal motifs, as well as turned vertical elements that resemble small columns. The side elevation shows the chest's structure supported by four rounded, bulbous legs. Each component is labeled with precise measurements in inches, indicating the width, height, and depth of both individual drawers and the entire chest. The text on the drawing includes the name "Lorenz Rothkranz," a reference to the Metropolitan Museum, and details identifying the chest of drawers as belonging to the Capen House, with a scale of 1/4 inch to 1 foot. Additional lines, numbers, and measurement notations appear throughout, detailing each segment of the chest's construction. The entire composition is neatly arranged and uniformly rendered in monochrome.
title: Chest of Drawers
